Academic & Departments
English as an additional language (EAL)
English as an additional language (EAL)
Papplewick welcomes pupils who speak English as an additional language (EAL) from different overseas countries. The EAL Department aims to help these pupils integrate successfully into the life of the school and access the academic curriculum. New pupils are given an English language test on entry and extra tuition may be recommended. Extra tuition is usually provided in one-to-one lessons, taught by specialist EAL teachers, but sometimes lessons can be in pairs and small groups.
Grammar and vocabulary development are key in EAL lessons, and the skills of reading, writing and speaking are catered for. Lessons are tailored to each pupil’s level and needs. The department can help prepare pupils for Cambridge language exams such as the B1 (Preliminary) and B2 (First) exams.
British Culture courses are run regularly by the department and aim to provide helpful background information about British history, geography and various aspects of British life that are often referred to in different subjects. These courses are fun, and boys on the most recent course enjoyed completing tasting notes for different British biscuits alongside more serious topics! It is important to note that whilst we focus on developing the boys’ English, their first languages and cultures are respected at all times.

About Papplewick
Academic & Departments
Academic & Departments
Papplewick is well known for its strength on the academic front while supporting those that may require some additional help. We have dedicated Form Teachers and Specialist teachers as well as a Learning Support and EAL department.
Class sizes average 13 boys per class. There is one class in Year 2, two classes in Year 3,4, and 5, increasing to three classes in each of Year 6, Year 7 and Year 8. Boys in Year 2-4 are primarily under the care of the Form Teacher, where there is a strong emphasis on reading, writing and basic numeracy. However, the curriculum also includes Science, French, History, Geography, TRP, Drama, Music, ICT, Art, P.E and DT, which are taught by our specialists. Latin is introduced to boys in Year 5 and by the time boys reach Year 6-8 all subjects are taught by specialist teachers and a formal scholarship 'set' is created to whom Greek is also taught. Schemes of work are designed with close reference to the National Curriculum, Common Entrance and Public School scholarship syllabuses. It is very much our belief that teachers should be there to inspire the boys and not just to be 'curriculum deliverers'.

About Papplewick
Charity and Outreach
Charity and Outreach
Charity and community outreach plays a very important part of Papplewick life. Our annual sponsored walk is a whole school event with families and friends invited to walk nearly ten miles around Windsor Great Park to raise money for a charity close to the heart of a student or one of their families. The most recent walk raised over £14,000 for Cardiac Risk in the Young (CRY).
In addition to regular charity events, part of the Thursday Afternoon activity programme (Charity Club) includes outreach work at a local Care Home where the boys entertain and talk to the residents, and exchange stories and play games. Students also support Alexander Devine Children's Hospice by undertaking a variety of jobs that support the Santa Dash and Summer Fair events.
An integral part of the Year 8 Leavers' Studies is participating in charity work to help local charities in any way they see fit. This year our Year 8 boys supported the Windsor Foodshare and Swings and Smiles, Thatcham. The boys gain a huge amount from these visits and the variety of work has a huge impact on local charities and its many volunteers.
The Stag Challenge is an annual expedition which enables a small number of boys to travel to the Eastern Cape of South Africa to carry out charitable work for the Ubunye Foundation. Each boy is tasked with planning and executing their own fundraising and all the money raised is donated to the foundation. This year we raised over £5,000 and the money has gone towards the 'Beautiful Toilet Project', which will enable the project visited to build an eco-toilet block that ensures the children that attend the community centre have access to safe and environmentally friendly toilets. The boys who take on the Stag Challenge are also given the opportunity to visit a project where they can visit the facilities, meet the staff and ultimately support the young children that access the services.

General Information
Governors
A.A.M. Try LL (Chair)
Andrew attended Papplewick from 1973-79, followed by Malvern College, before graduating from Northeastern University in Boston, USA. Born into an entrepreneurial Windsor family, Andrew has followed the family tradition and created, grown, and sold a number of businesses. Andrew’s main venture is ComXo, which provides on-demand virtualised back office services to some of the largest professional services firms in the City. Andrew is passionate about his home town Windsor, and participates in a number of local Societies including Trustee of The Windsor Festival, Chairman of the Royal Windsor Rose and Horticultural Society. Andrew is also a trustee of the Windsor Learning Partnership Multi Academy Trust and served as governor of the Berkshire College of Agriculture for 8 years. He is a trustee of the Prince Philip Trust and was appointed as a Deputy Lieutenant for Berkshire in October 2019, and became Lord Lieutenant for Berkshire in October 2023.
John is a Chartered Surveyor and Managing Director of The Frost Partnership, a private family firm. He is a keen sportsman and traveller. An Old Papplewickian, he became a Governor in 2011.
Tobi has worked in cyber-security for 16 years as a sales professional with a broad range of experience selling technology solutions and consultancy services into a range of industries. His specialties include Security, Networking, Design and Build, Managed Services and Outsourcing, and he has been working for Cisco since 2022. His son went to Papplewick and he became a Governor in 2024.
Tim’s career started in brand marketing, developing into general management. During this time he worked in various countries in the Americas and Europe. He is active now in his family’s equestrian business, and with fundraising activities for the Conservative party and the Carlton Club. All three of his sons were at Papplewick and he became a Governor in 2010.
Andrew served as a Master at Harrow School for three decades. He was House Master of The Head Master’s House before his promotion to Harrow’s Senior Management Team in September 2012. As Senior Tutor he oversaw safeguarding and child protection as well as other areas of pastoral care and pupil welfare. Andrew taught Classics but maintains a keen interest in sport, drama and music (in particular the choral tradition). He became a Governor in 2017 and took over as Safeguarding Governor in April 2018.
Revd. Dr. B.G. McNair-Scott
Benji is an ordained Church of England priest who has been working as a chaplain and teacher at St Catherine’s school, Bramley since 2012. He lives in Guildford with his wife and four children and is a published author and keen sportsman. He became a governor in 2019.
Simon qualified as a solicitor after studying law at Oxford University and practised in the City of London. He then switched careers to specialise in learning and development and obtained an MSc in Human Resources and is a qualified coach. After a series of senior learning and development, HR and knowledge management roles with large international law firms, Simon now runs his own consultancy where he focuses on coaching, training and facilitation. Simon has a keen interest in sport and history and lives in North London with his wife, two children and a black labrador. Simon has been a Governor since 2011.

About Papplewick
Academic & Departments
Learning Support
Learning Support
Papplewick is committed to developing the talents, and meeting the educational needs, of all our pupils and ensuring that they make progress. We recognise that some boys may find learning harder than others and may therefore require some support in their learning.
Boys are first identified through a comprehensive process that involves input from previous schools, staff and parents, initial testing and formal assessment. Our Head of Learning Support is able to carry out observations and assessments to determine suitable interventions. Once a specific need has been identified, any boy in need of support, typically in either English or Maths, is allocated a specialist learning support tutor who will provide individual or small group support in our well-resourced department within the school.
For boys with more complex needs, the advice of an educational psychologist or medical professional may be sought. Such advice then provides the bedrock for informing staff about an individual pupil's particular educational needs to enable us to support your child to develop strategies and build on their strengths and confidence in order to achieve their personal potential.

About Papplewick
Parents of Papplewick (POP)
Parents of Papplewick (POP)
Welcome
Welcome to Parents of Papplewick, or POP as we are more commonly known. Run by a number of parents we are a forum responsible for organising all parent/staff social events such as the MacMillan Coffee Morning, Pub Quiz Night, Wine Tasting Evening, Hog Roast, and the end of year Summer Ball. Everyone is welcome to come along to a POP meeting, generate new ideas and help to run or coordinate an event. If you would like to get involved - your level of commitment is down to you and your availability - please email us at pop@papplewick.org.uk and we will get in touch.
Macmillan Coffee Morning
We start the new school year with our annual Macmillan Coffee Morning, held on one of the Saturdays in September. The baked goods – whether shop-bought or homemade, sweet or savoury – are generously donated by our wonderful school community. This Saturday afternoon is a great opportunity to catch up with friends, meet new parents, and come together in support of a very worthwhile cause.
The Pub Quiz is an unforgettable evening hosted by the brilliant professional quizmaster, Lesley Brewis, who is ready to challenge your brains with a mix of intriguing and amusing questions. It is a night of fun, laughter and friendly competition, accompanied by a mouth-watering curry dinner. Our much-loved round of true-or-false questions about the teachers is guaranteed to deliver plenty of laughs and a few surprises!
The Wine Tasting makes its comeback in February. The doors open at 7.00pm, with a glass of prosecco on arrival, followed by a tasting experience of Italian wines, each carefully paired with matched canapés and Italian nibbles. An engaging wine tasting talk by an award-winning sommelier, along with fun games and quizzes, promises a truly memorable evening.
The Hog Roast for the boys is one of the most eagerly anticipated and popular events in the school calendar. The sun miraculously always seems to shine, and there is plenty of fun for the children, including (but certainly not limited to) Land Zorbs, Laser Quest and the Bungee Run, as well as popcorn, ice creams and candy floss. It truly is an event for the whole family – there is even a Papplewick Dog Show, giving the family pooch the chance to sashay around the show ring. For the adults, there’s afternoon tea, the ever-popular hamper raffle, and a couple of cricket matches to enjoy, including the much-loved Year 4 mums versus sons match. A sumptuous barbecue lunch is served, featuring the eponymous hog, burgers, vegan sausages and delicious salads. Gates open at 12 noon, with festivities winding down at around 4.00pm.
The hottest ticket in town, the Papplewick Summer Ball is a black-tie event that gives everyone the chance to dress up and celebrate the end of the school year in style. The evening begins with prosecco and canapés on the Bursar's Lawn, followed by a three-course dinner and plenty of dancing. The marquee opens at 7.00pm, with carriages at midnight.

School Trips and Tours
School Trips and Tours
Regular tours abroad are a special feature of Papplewick, whether it be for sporting, charitable, academic, or cultural reasons.
The school organises a week of total immersion in French for Year 7 boys in Burgundy, an annual ski trip to Europe (which includes families), Choir Trips to Europe and within the UK, Adventure Trips to South Africa, and a Leavers’ Camp to Spain for Year 8 boys. Major sports (alternating cricket, rugby, and football) tours also take place every year to such countries as South Africa, Argentina, St.Lucia, and Spain.
In addition, all boys enjoy a variety of educational trips and outings during the course of the year to plays, concerts, and places of historical or geographical interest, often taking advantage of all that London has to offer.

About Papplewick
Chapel
Whether by design or by circumstance, the Chapel is physically open to the school hall and a major thoroughfare. In many ways, this symbolises the fact that it is open to people of all faiths and of none.
We gather together for a daily act of worship, which also provides the school community with a meeting place and a start to the working day. Our simple act of worship always includes a hymn, reading and prayer, as well as a homily offering a thought for the day applicable to the whole community delivered both by staff and by boys.
On Saturdays, we celebrate our weekly service and welcome families and friends to share this with us. As a school, we are proud of our strong choral tradition and our four-part First Choir, comprised of boys, staff and parents, adds a different spiritual dimension to our worship. We frequently welcome visiting preachers at these services, drawn from many senior schools. Boys take an active part in all our worship and we are known for our enthusiastic congregational singing!

About Papplewick
Academic & Departments
Library
Papplewick’s Senior library for Years 5 – 8 is very popular with boys either looking for the latest publication from a favourite author or searching the non fiction titles to help with research for lesson projects or prep.
The library is very well stocked with both fiction and non-fiction titles. The fiction books include classic and modern titles, and sets or series. Non-fiction books include many science, history and arts titles, and a good selection of biographies.
The school Librarian is helped by a rota of pupil librarians who may apply for the post when a vacancy arises. After a short interview with the Librarian, when she is assured that they are naturally very tidy boys and will, therefore, help keep the school library spick and span, they are appointed to the role. Their duties include helping to choose new titles for the library, preparing new books for the shelves, and chasing overdue books.
We have visits from authors most terms. These give pupils the opportunity to listen to presentations and then to meet and talk with the author who will sign books for them. Past author visits to school include Michael Grant, Sophie McKenzie, Robin Jarvis, Simon Mayo, Paul Stewart and Chris Riddell.
A Junior library is situated along the Junior corridor which contains suitable books for Years 2 – 4.
The Accelerated Reader Scheme is used across the entire school to encourage all boys to read for pleasure.
